fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Turnaround Space; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reach the residence.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point, particularly at night.
• Trim back dense vegetation along the driveway so approaching vehicles have a clear line of sight to the residence.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure to keep walls and rooflines visible and reachable from the outside.
• Clear a turning area near the residence or detached structure large enough for an emergency vehicle to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Keep a pedestrian path open along at least one side of the residence to allow responders to move between the front and rear on foot.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without obstruction.
• Post the property address visibly at the street, facing the direction of approaching traffic.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Large Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Mixed Vegetation; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Along Driveway
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees near the house, cutting them up to about 10 feet from the ground.
• Clear shrubs and small plants growing beneath the large trees so fire cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Separate the mixed vegetation growing close to the structure by removing individual plants to create open bare or grassy gaps.
• Cut back or remove shrubs and overhanging branches along both sides of the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, leaves, and debris that could block emergency vehicle access.
• Clear vegetation along the rear of the property to open a path for movement around the back of the structure.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from within the scattered shrub areas nearest to the house.
• Thin scattered trees across the property so individual trees are not close enough to carry fire directly toward the structure.
• Keep the ground beneath trees and shrubs near the house raked clear of dry leaves, needles, and fallen branches.
